strategies.agent-0: Side draws: look for middle cuts (for example blends) that a side draw can deliver from one column instead of two.
strategies.agent-1: Energy-lean columns: more stages and lower reflux and boil-up to cut energy, the largest cost at these prices.
strategies.agent-2: Direct sequence: take the lightest components off first, one split at a time, working down the volatility order.
strategies.agent-3: Middle-out: make the first split in the middle of the volatility range, then work outwards on both sides.
strategies.agent-4: Premium-heavy: push the most valuable products to 99% purity to earn the premium grade.
strategies.agent-5: Blend-heavy: sell the C3, C4, C5 and C6 mixtures as blends instead of separating their close-boiling members.
strategies.agent-6: Double effects: look for close splits where a double-effect column saves enough energy to pay for the second column.
strategies.agent-7: Indirect sequence: take the heaviest components off first, working up the volatility order.
strategies.agent-8: Pressure-staged: use the valves' pressure drops to keep condensers out of expensive refrigeration.
strategies.agent-9: Lean plant: few columns, sell only the most valuable products, keep energy use low.
